title: Mercurys Boot & Baal Bone Gap
lede: A short walk with a bit of bushbashing to a boot-shaped rock on the Capertee cliffline, which you can climb from the toe.
description: A short walk with some bushbashing to Mercurys Boot, a boot-shaped sandstone rock on the Capertee cliffline near Baal Bone Gap in Gardens of Stone National Park.
hero_alt: A bushwalker standing on top of Mercurys Boot, a boot-shaped sandstone rock on the Capertee cliffline

card.image_alt: A walker on top of Mercurys Boot
card.blurb: A short walk with a bit of bushbashing to a boot-shaped rock on the Capertee cliffline. Climb it from the toe.

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Capertee Valley rim, near Ben Bullen

intro: High above the Capertee Valley, a great sandstone block leans out over the drop. From the right angle it looks just like a boot. It's a short walk with a bit of bushbashing, and you can climb right up onto the Boot from the toe.

getting_there.intro: There are two ways in: along the ridge from Moffitts Trail, or up from Baal Bone Gap. Both are short, and both finish with a bit of bushbashing to the cliffline.

options.heading: Moffitts Trail ridge
options.text:
Head for Moffitts Trail (also signposted as Ben Bullen Trail) and leave it on the ridge at Ben Bullen GR [X]. Conventional vehicles should stop wherever the track starts to look too rough for them.

From the ridge, bushbash out to the cliffline and follow it to the Boot.

options.heading: Baal Bone Gap
options.text: Baal Bone Gap is a natural break in the cliffs just below the Boot. From the Gap, climb up to the cliffline and follow it west to the Boot.

getting_there.note: Fire trail conditions change quickly after rain. Check the current NPWS alerts for Gardens of Stone National Park before you go.

walk_intro: There's no formed track to the Boot. Expect some scrub and rock platforms, with the cliffline as your guide.

stops.heading: Moffitts Trail or Baal Bone Gap
stops.text: Start from the ridge off Moffitts Trail, or from Baal Bone Gap. Either way, head for the cliff edge above the Capertee Valley.

stops.heading: Bushbash to the cliffline
stops.text: The last stretch is a bit of a bushbash through the scrub. Once you reach the cliffline, follow it and the views open up over the Capertee Valley.

stops.heading: Mercurys Boot
stops.text:
You'll know the Boot when you see it: a big rock jutting out over the valley, shaped unmistakably like a boot.

You can climb onto it from the toe. Take care on top, because it's a long way down on the valley side. And make sure you get a kicking picture before you leave.
stops.image_alt: A walker standing on top of Mercurys Boot against a clear blue sky
stops.caption: Standing on top of Mercurys Boot, high above the Capertee Valley

stops.heading: Back the way you came
stops.text: Retrace your steps along the cliffline and back through the scrub to your car.

tips.heading: Off-track navigation
tips.text: There's no track or signs to the Boot. Carry a map and compass or GPS, and know how to use them.

tips.heading: Cliff edges
tips.text: The cliffs are high and sheer, and the edges can be undercut. Take care climbing the Boot, and keep well back from the edge, especially with children or in wind.

tips.heading: Water
tips.text: Don't count on finding any. There may be water in a pipe at Baal Bone Gap, but the tap may be locked, so carry all you'll need.

tips.heading: Respect the Country
tips.text: Baal Bone Gap has Aboriginal cultural sites, including hand stencils. Look, but don't touch. Leave no trace.

tips.heading: Tell someone
tips.text: Leave your plans with someone, and think about carrying a PLB. There's very little phone coverage out there.
